findings.description: Invite codes are bearer secrets that grant workspace membership, but they are generated with `random.choices`, which uses the Mersenne Twister. Its output is predictable once enough outputs are observed. An attacker who sees a few codes can predict others and join workspaces uninvited.
findings.suggestion: Use the `secrets` module, e.g. `"".join(secrets.choice(CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(CODE_LENGTH))`, or `secrets.token_urlsafe`.
findings.title: Invite codes generated with non-cryptographic PRNG

findings.description: `accept` rejects revoked or exhausted links but never checks `expires_at`. It does not call `is_active(now)`. An expired link can still be used to join the workspace, which defeats the TTL.
findings.title: accept() does not check link expiry

findings.description: If the actor created the link, the manager check is skipped. A creator who has since been demoted or removed from the workspace can still revoke the link. It would be safer to require current manager status, or at least membership, for everyone.
findings.suggestion: Always call `require_manager`, or at minimum check current membership for the creator.
findings.title: Link creator can revoke without being a manager any more

findings.description: `accept` adds the user with `link.role` without re-checking that the creator is still a manager. A link created by an admin who was later demoted or removed keeps granting ADMIN access to new members.
findings.suggestion: On accept, verify that `link.created_by` is still a manager in the workspace, or revoke the creator's links when their role changes.
findings.title: Link role can exceed what the creator may now grant, and accept uses stored role unchecked
